learning_outcomes.text: Students who have successfully completed this module will have a fundamental understanding of the structure-property relationships of engineering materials based on metals.

Students who have successfully completed this module will have expanded their knowledge of elastic and plastic properties to the material microstructure, so that they can trace these back to the atomic spacing potential curve and dislocation movement. Furthermore, they will know the basic methodology by which the suitability of components for application under complex mechanical stress can be estimated.

Students who have successfully completed this module are able to specifically use the methods of mechanical material testing and analysis to determine the suitability of metallic materials for forming processes as well as for structural applications.

Students prepare the results obtained from practical experiments in a team. Subsequently, the results are discussed taking into account the learned material and supplementary specialist literature and communicated in an appropriate form.

syllabus_topics: Plasticity – Dislocations (Types and Energy, Slip Systems, Schmid's Law of Shear Stress, Dislocation Movement, Interactions with Barriers)
Plasticity – Hardening Behavior (Hardening Stages for Mono- and Polycrystals, Influencing Factors, Forming Technology Characteristics)
In-depth analysis of Strengthening Mechanisms (Solid Solution Hardening, Precipitation Hardening, Work Hardening, Grain Refinement Hardening)
Fracture Mechanics (Stress Field at Cracks, Crack Propagation, Fracture Mechanical Material Characteristics)
Material Fatigue (Testing Techniques, Stress-Strain Hysteresis, Wöhler Diagram, Fatigue Damage, Increasing Fatigue Strength)
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is an oral examination. An ungraded experimental work is also required, corresponding to the scope of laboratory activities (4-6 experiments).
